question: Which ATT&CK techniques do CAPEC-37, CAPEC-639 map to (they overlap), and what mitigations apply to the deduplicated union?

answer.headline: Gathered 8 record(s) from 2 source(s); 6 cross-source correlation(s) on shared identifiers.
answer.narrative: CAPEC-639 maps to ATT&CK techniques T1552.001, T1552.003, T1552.004, T1552.006, and T1039, while CAPEC-37 maps to T1005 and T1552.004. The deduplicated union of these techniques is T1552.001, T1552.003, T1552.004, T1552.006, T1039, and T1005. The mitigations for this union are M1057, M1041, M1047, M1022, M1027, M1028, M1017, M1051, and M1015.

records.name: Probe System Files
records.label: AttackPattern
records.description: An adversary obtains unauthorized information due to improperly protected files. If an application stores sensitive information in a file that is not protected by proper access control, then an adversary can access the file and search for sensitive information.

records.name: Retrieve Embedded Sensitive Data
records.label: AttackPattern
records.description: An attacker examines a target system to find sensitive data that has been embedded within it. This information can reveal confidential contents, such as account numbers or individual keys/credentials that can be used as an intermediate step in a larger attack.

results.sub_question: What mitigations does ATT&CK list for those mapped techniques?
results.query: MATCH (t) WHERE (t:Technique OR t:SubTechnique) AND t.attack_id IN $ids OPTIONAL MATCH (t)<-[:MITIGATES]-(m:Mitigation) RETURN t.attack_id AS technique_id, t.name AS technique_name, m.attack_id AS mitigation_id, m.name AS mitigation_name LIMIT 300
